unmapped_findings: Room-temperature tensile yield stress and total elongation for Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C are reported as '-' (not determined) in Table 2, so no tensile strength/ductility values are available for this as-cast sample.

Fracture mode of Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C at room temperature is IGD+TGC (intergranular decohesion + transgranular cleavage); the SEM fractograph (Fig. 4l) shows partially intergranular (smooth) and partially transgranular (facetted) fracture.

In elevated-temperature compression tests, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C (like other Nb/Ta-containing Fe-26Al alloys) shows its yield-stress-anomaly peak shifted towards lower temperatures and higher stresses compared with binary Fe-26Al; no numeric peak temperature/stress is reported for this specific alloy.

At 650 °C and 800 °C, the compressive yield stress of Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C exceeds its tensile yield stress, consistent with the tension-compression asymmetry reported for all investigated alloys (Figs. 7 and 8).
Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C is one of the Nb/Ta-containing alloys reported to show the highest strengthening effects at room temperature and at elevated temperatures relative to other Fe-Al-M-C alloys.
